newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian stocks soar on BNI listing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian stocks soar on BNI listing.

text.p: Giant state-owned Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) was listed locally on Monday after one of the country's best-received floats, propelling turnover to near-record levels and sending the index surging.
The index closed 2.51 percent higher at 628.24 points on a sharp inflow of funds following the listing of BNI, brokers said.

"It was widely expected that the BNI listing would enliven Jakarta stocks. I think it (the boom) will last until the second week of December before the market slows down for the Christmas holiday," a foreign broker said.
Brokers said that strong buying interest in BNI had sparked extremely positive sentiment and also triggered a rise in other banking stocks and issues with sound fundamentals.
"Some fresh funds came into the market and fundamentally sound and liquid stocks benefited," an analyst from a Hong Kong-based securities firm said.
BNI closed at 1,250 rupiah against an offer price of 850 rupiah and topped the active list with a staggering 179.33 million shares traded. It had risen to 1,300 rupiah earlier.
BNI accounted for more than half the shares traded on the exchange on Monday. The turnover is the among the highest ever recorded in Jakarta, exchange officials said.
A total of 4.34 billion BNI shares were listed on the Jakarta and Surabaya stock exchanges on Monday.
The bank offered one-fourth of its equity, about 1.08 billion shares, to the public during the offer period from November 4 to 7.

On November 15, PT Danareksa Sekuritas, the lead underwriter, announced that the stock was oversubscribed 4.46 times during the public offer. The response is considered to be among the best in the government's ongoing programme of partially privatising state-owned corporations.
Brokers said trading in BNI was dominated by local investors while foreign investors seemed restrained on the perception the price was too high.

"Most foreigners continue to trade on fundamental aspects and from that point of view, the current price of BNI is too expensive. Usually investors compare it to Bank International Indonesia, which is the blue-chip in the banking sector," a foreign broker said.
However, brokers said, they believed the stock could hover between 1,200 to 1,300 rupiah during the first week of the listing on the strong support shown by local investors.
"Based on fundamental aspects, the fair price for BNI is between 1,100 to 1,150 rupiah," said Mirza Adityaswara, a banking analyst at BZW Niaga Securities.
Adityaswara said foreign investors' sentiment toward BNI was not as strong as local investors as the stock has not yet been included in the Morgan Stanley Composite Index (MSCI).
"It is widely predicted that BNI will be included in the MSCI but as long as they have not included it yet, foreign investors will continue trading on fundamental aspects," Adityaswara added.
